At table construction the source lane receives selected.metadataRead. The outer epoch also holds that selected object. A future single graph invocation may deduplicate this exact shared node; if the actual table graph falls back or lane differs, no such node sharing is available. Static code demonstrates the intended identity edge, not timing, invocation counts or full-owner success.

Legacy, table, inventory, title, checker and browser factories instantiate their own owner/lane/tool objects and can each instantiate further independent owners. Examples: inventory builds its own legacyTools, its own checker context and its own browser context; checker context constructs checker owner and a separate checker source; browser context constructs browser owner and browser source proposal, with the proposal/source building additional browser owners. These are actual independent instances, not deduplicable by equal path, reader or owner label.

Same-instance reuse exists only within one original epoch wrapper or inside a genuine registered lane; separate freshly constructed contexts and operations remain distinct. CJS/source guard constructors, fresh semantic source reviews, inventory helper workflow and checker/browser verifier subprocesses are real construction work, not scheduler guard calls or results to cache.
